questions.q: Why did Solomon ask Hiram to send him cedar logs as he did for his father David?
questions.a: Solomon asked Hiram to send him cedar logs so he could build a house for Yahweh’s name and a palace for his kingdom.

questions.q: Why did Solomon plan to build a house for the name of Yahweh that would be very large?
questions.a: Solomon planned to build a large house for the name of Yahweh because his God was greater than all other gods.

questions.q: Who did Solomon need if he was to build a house for the name of Yahweh which reflected Yahweh’s greatness?
questions.a: Solomon needed a man who was skilled at work in gold, sliver, bronze, iron, and in purple, crimson, blue wool and who could make all kinds of engraved wood.

questions.q: Why did Solomon want Hiram to send him cedar, fir, and algum trees from Lebanon?
questions.a: Solomon wanted Hiram to send these trees to him so that the house which he would build for the name of Yahweh would be great and marvelous.

questions.q: According to Hiram, why did Yahweh make Solomon the king over the people of Israel?
questions.a: According to Hiram, Yahweh made Solomon the king because Yahweh loved his people and Solomon was gifted with prudence and understanding.

questions.q: Why did Hiram send Huramabi to Solomon?
questions.a: Hiram sent Hurambi because he was skilled at work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and in timber, and in purple, blue, crimson wool, and fine linen as well as in making any kind of engravings.

questions.q: How was it possible for the wood from Lebanon to be taken to Israel?
questions.a: The wood from Lebanon was taken to Israel as rafts by sea to Joppa and then carried up to Jerusalem.

commentary.text: Solomon's message to Huram respecting the temple, His treaty with Huram.

—Solomon informs Huram of the particular services to be performed in the temple. The mysteries of the true religion, unlike those of the Gentile superstitions, sought not concealment. Solomon endeavoured to possess Huram with great and high thoughts of the God of Israel. We should not be afraid or ashamed to embrace every opportunity to speak of God, and to impress others with a deep sense of the importance of his favour and service. Now that the people of Israel kept close to the law and worship of God, the neighbouring nations were willing to be taught by them in the true religion, as the Israelites had been willing in the days of their apostacy, to be infected with the idolatries and superstitions of their neighbours. A wise and pious king is an evidence of the Lord's special love for his people. How great then was God's love to his believing people, in giving his only-begotten Son to be their Prince and their Saviour.
